expectations.text: Recommends against the sales reporting line.
expectations.evidence: "Don't move the reporting line to sales. Counter-propose: keep the line, take the two heads, give sales a strict interlock instead."

expectations.text: Names attribution speed and pipeline visibility as what the sales line genuinely optimizes.
expectations.evidence: "**Optimizes** attribution speed, pipeline visibility."

expectations.text: Names trust, community, and any work with a horizon longer than the quarter as what the sales line starves.

expectations.text: Proposes placing the team in product or marketing and giving sales a service interlock instead of the reporting line.
expectations.evidence: "DevRel stays under `[product marketing / product — pick the one that actually owns developer adoption today]`... Sales gets a service interlock for pipeline visibility instead of the reporting line."

expectations.text: Sets the sales interlock mode to X-as-a-service.
expectations.evidence: "Cap the sales interlock in hours up front — e.g. 4 hours/week per head, X-as-a-service only: evaluation material out, field objections in."

expectations.text: States what crosses that boundary: evaluation material out, field objections in.
expectations.evidence: "X-as-a-service only: evaluation material out, field objections in."

expectations.text: Names an arbiter for the sales interlock.
expectations.evidence: The closest language is "roles titled around sales-facing work..., managed inside DevRel's existing line" and "no surface gets a lead-gen gate added without your sign-off" — neither explicitly designates a named arbiter/approver role for the sales interlock itself.

expectations.text: Proposes an observable cap on the sales interlock's load, such as hours per week.

expectations.text: Adds a re-org trigger tied to that interlock breaching its cap or staying in collaboration mode past its end.
expectations.evidence: The only automatic triggers given are "if community engagement or non-sales content output drops for two consecutive months, the line reopens for discussion automatically" and a general "Fixed review date — one quarter out" — neither is tied to the interlock exceeding its hour cap or overrunning its collaboration-mode duration.
